analysis.title: GS Crook - GS MORNING 1) New Fed Call, 2) France Update, 3) ISM Preview, 4) KT on Brazil and 5) Tail Hedging Ideas 1 Oct 2026
key_insights: Core PCE prices rose 0.25% in August, somewhat below expectations. The year-over-year rate is 3.01%, well below expectations. The downward revision from the methodological changes was larger than GS expected and mostly came from the portfolio management component.

GS now expects core PCE of 3.0% on a Q4/Q4 basis, against the median FOMC participant forecast of 3.4%. Together with comments from NY Fed President Williams, GS thinks an October hike is unlikely. It pushes the second hike in its forecast to December and sees a strong chance the FOMC concludes further hikes are unnecessary.

GS FX strategy (Jenkins) notes an October hike is still priced roughly 50-50 even though GS no longer calls for it. He sees room for that pricing to move and is watching Fed speakers for recognition of the better post-revision inflation data, with Waller speaking later today.

France presents its budget today, aiming for a 5% deficit next year versus 5.4% expected this year. GS expects the actual outturn to be 5.3%. GS Econ does not expect new information relative to Lecornu's interview two weeks ago. The more important event is RN's counter-proposal due next Tuesday, which will show what concessions it wants and its economic plans if it wins.
The French budget process is expected to be drawn out, potentially lasting until mid-December or early next year. Acute market stress could force parties to a quicker compromise.

GS Econ projects French debt/GDP rising to 125% at the start of next decade. The average interest rate rises to 3% from 2%. Stabilising debt needs a +1% primary balance on GS market forecasts, a level France has rarely achieved (95th percentile over 35 years). At market rates it would need a 2% primary surplus, which has never been achieved.

The recent OAT-Bund widening did not come from fundamental news. Current-quarter growth tracking is stable at 0.1%, the deficit and budget news matched expectations, and polls were stable. GS points to the difficult backdrop in energy and rates, election uncertainty and Melenchon rising to second place in first-round polls. GS simulations give him little chance of winning the second round, but his proposal to cancel French debt held at Banque de France is a deep tail that could move markets even on a small probability shift.

GS estimates ISM manufacturing was unchanged at 54.6 in September. Residual seasonality and a 0.6pt decline in GS's manufacturing survey tracker to 56.1 are offset by convergence toward the level implied by other manufacturing surveys, which the ISM is currently below. The market is likely to focus on it after last week's strong S&P PMI beat.

GS trackers suggest the manufacturing PMI is now roughly in line with other manufacturing surveys. The services PMI stands much higher than other services surveys and is likely to normalize in upcoming readings.

GS EM FX strategy (Trivedi) says EM assets are stuck between rates and oil. Lower energy prices are needed for lasting local rates relief, and GS recommends a selective approach focused on idiosyncratic stories. Brazil's general elections on Sunday October 4 are the next one.

GS sees Brazilian local rates as offering the best asymmetry into the vote, given a wide fiscal deficit, high nominal and real rates and elevated premium across the DI swap and local bond curves. A fiscally unfriendly result could cause a knee-jerk sell-off, but GS expects it to be more contained than the rally from a market-friendly result. Risk-reward favours receiving the belly of the DI curve.

On BRL, GS's cyclical fair value model puts USD/BRL at 4.80 if the residual fiscal premium from the 2024 depreciation episode fully compresses. A negative fiscal outcome would mean 5.80 (December 2024 premium) or 5.40 (September 2024 premium).

Brazilian equities: Bovespa is up 10% from mid-August lows, but domestic equities ex-commodity exporters, rate-sensitive stocks and small-caps are flat to down YTD. Rate-sensitive stocks have rate beta 2-3x the index and trade at about 10x, -0.9 s.d. vs 10-year history. GS says rate-sensitive stocks and index call-spreads offer the most attractive risk-reward.

GS FX Sales (Wade) says the backdrop is higher energy prices, elevated core yields and sustained AI investment. Front-end rate vol and a higher-for-longer yield path have hurt macro investors, while in FX a rangebound USD, low vol and diminished correlations keep carry on top. Wade's read from conversations is that almost nobody is hedged and hedging is cheap, with persistent energy prices and yields the key downside risk.
Tail hedge ideas from GS FX Sales: a Brent Dec26 $120 call, a 6m AUDUSD digital put and a 1y dual binary on SPX and 2y SOFR. Pricing is indicative.

tension_points.bull_case: A market-friendly result could drive a rally in local rates and rate-sensitive equities, helped by a DI curve that has overshot fundamentals for two years and a potential virtuous monetary-fiscal cycle.
tension_points.bear_case: A fiscally unfriendly outcome could trigger a knee-jerk sell-off against a wide fiscal deficit and elevated premium, with USD/BRL at 5.40 to 5.80 under a negative fiscal outcome.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A fiscally unfriendly result in the October 4 general elections.
